This is load-bearing, not debug-only — it's the base dir for `resolve(dbgProjectDir, rawPath)` which turns relative paths into absolute (the core fix of this PR). The `dbg` prefix invites removal in a future cleanup. If someone drops it and only keeps the `hookDebug` calls, relative-path resolution breaks again silently.

```suggestion
const projectDir = resolveProjectDirFromHook(import.meta.url);
```

This fixes the adapter's own child, but the child (a core hook) inherits this env, including the stripped PATH — `runCore` passes no `env`. So when `stop.ts`/`sync-statusline.ts`/`runtime-compile.ts` then spawn bare `"bun"`, they ENOENT in the exact case this PR targets. If you want the stop guard and statusline to actually come back (as the CHANGELOG claims), you'd need to pass an `env` with bun's dir on PATH here, or thread `process.execPath` down. Fine as a follow-up — just don't want the CHANGELOG saying those layers are restored when they aren't.
